# Canada Work Permit Renewal Prep

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/briefcase.svg

You already have several core documents in hand, so the main job over the next 8 weeks is organizing, checking expiry dates, and filling any gaps early. I’m treating this as a practical preparation checklist, not legal advice.

## Document Checklist and 8-Week Plan

### Core documents to gather
- **Passport**: valid until **2028-07-15**; keep a scan of the photo page and any stamped pages.
- **Current work permit**: front and back copy.
- **Employer letter**: current, signed, and on company letterhead.
- **Pay stubs**: last **6 months**; organize newest to oldest.
- **Job proof**: recent offer letter, employment confirmation, or role description if available.
- **Spouse documents**: spouse’s open work permit copy, passport copy, and marriage/common-law proof if relevant.
- **Identity documents**: any prior permits, visitor records, or status documents.
- **Digital copies**: PDF scans named clearly and stored in one folder.
- **Photos**: only if your application checklist later asks for them.

### Helpful supporting items
- **Employment details**: job title, start date, salary, work location, manager contact.
- **Travel history**: recent trips and entry dates if you need to reference them.
- **Address history**: current address and any changes since your last permit.
- **Family details**: spouse’s status information ready in one place.
- **Calendar reminders**: expiry date and internal deadlines.

### 8-week task timeline
| Week | Focus | Tasks | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Organize files | Create one folder; scan passport, permit, employer letter, pay stubs; label files clearly | Clean document set |
| 2 | Check dates | Confirm passport validity, permit expiry, spouse permit details, and any document freshness issues | Expiry tracker |
| 3 | Fill gaps | Request updated employer letter or HR confirmation if wording is weak or outdated | Stronger employer package |
| 4 | Review employment proof | Sort pay stubs, add job offer or confirmation, note role and compensation details | Employment evidence bundle |
| 5 | Family status prep | Gather spouse permit copy and relationship proof; keep them in one subfolder | Family-status packet |
| 6 | Application readiness | Build a checklist of forms, signatures, and upload files; verify PDF quality | Draft-ready package |
| 7 | Final review | Check naming, page order, legibility, and consistency across documents | Submission-ready set |
| 8 | Buffer week | Fix missing items, re-scan anything unclear, and keep copies backed up | Final backup package |

### Common mistakes to avoid
- Waiting until the last two weeks to organize documents.
- Uploading blurry scans or cropped pages.
- Using inconsistent dates, job titles, or addresses across documents.
- Forgetting the spouse’s permit copy or relationship documents.
- Leaving pay stubs unsorted or missing months.
- Assuming an employer letter is enough without supporting pay records.
- Mixing old and current permits in the same file without labels.
- Not keeping backup copies in cloud storage and offline storage.
- Ignoring passport validity when planning the permit timing.
- Submitting documents with pages missing, rotated, or unreadable.

## Practical Preparation Checklist

### Ready-to-use document order
- 1. Passport copy
- 2. Current work permit copy
- 3. Employer letter
- 4. Pay stubs, newest first
- 5. Job offer or role confirmation
- 6. Spouse open work permit copy
- 7. Marriage/common-law proof, if needed
- 8. Any prior status documents
- 9. Address/contact history
- 10. Backup scans of everything

### Quality checks before submission
- File names are clear and consistent.
- Every scan is readable on a phone screen.
- Dates match across documents.
- All pages are included.
- PDFs open correctly before upload.
- You have one backup copy of the full package.
